evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析 / 子 / form and function history
evidence.text: The page distinguishes two Shang forms: 𢀈, described as a newborn with hair and two legs, and 子, emphasizing a large infant head, moving arms, and undeveloped legs; it identifies the graph’s original sense as “infant.” It reports the more complex form for the first earthly branch and its replacement by 子 after the beginning of Zhou, while 子 also represented a child and the sixth branch, later written 巳. It cites Heji 94 有子 as a pregnancy-related example and describes later clan-leader, loan, suffix, and ‘young’ uses. These are the database’s interpretations and reported attestations, not direct readings independently verified here.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 子-seal.svg as a vector depiction of 子 in Shuowen seal-script style. It names Sinica, hanziyuan, CUHK and other databases as available character sources and cites hanziyuan image s10971 for this drawing. The page describes a digital file made with Inkscape; it is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:子-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: File description / original file, licensing and history
evidence.text: The inspected file page links its original SVG at https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/89/%E5%AD%90-seal.svg. It states the image representation is released to the public domain and records an upload on 11 April 2007. The browser could not render the SVG itself, so its pixels were not visually inspected in this research.
evidence.title: File:子-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The exact file page links separate files for Shang oracle, Shang bronze, Western Zhou, Warring States, Chu slips, Qin slips, and Shuowen seal forms. This confirms that the selected seal drawing is one modern-rendered stage among distinct labeled candidates; the seal image does not itself document the Shang pictograph.
evidence.title: File:子-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: Search result character record 子.6 / image metadata
evidence.text: Search results exposed a character-specific Xiaoxuetang record labeled 子.6. The character page itself returned a cache-miss access failure when opened, so the period, exact form label and direct rendered glyph URL could not be verified for a usable image candidate.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形

search_audit.query: 子 oracle bone bronze inscriptions infant graph form evolution child earliest attestation CUHK; 子 seal script ancient forms Wikimedia Commons 子-seal.svg; site:xiaoxue.iis.sinica.edu.tw 子 字形演變 子 甲骨文
search_audit.outcome: Opened the CUHK character analysis, exact Commons file description page, and Xiaoxuetang record. CUHK describes the competing/overlapping Shang graph uses; Commons establishes the seal-form image identity, source attribution, direct original-file link and public-domain claim. Direct SVG rendering failed in the browser; the Xiaoxuetang character record returned a cache miss.

search_audit.query: site:xiaoxue.iis.sinica.edu.tw 子 字形演變 甲骨 金文 小篆; Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang rights CC0 glyph attribute notice
search_audit.outcome: Search results surfaced a 子.6 record and Xiaoxuetang search interface. The queried Xiaoxuetang subpage was not accessible in its open call, and the official CC0 notice for the relevant single-character images/attributes was not verified; the other notice found concerned a different Academia Sinica system and was not applied to Xiaoxuetang.

gaps: The exact date of the earliest child-sense inscription was not established. The CUHK page reports Shang examples and inscription references but no independently verified calendar date for the earliest 子 child token.
The paleographic account supports a pictorial infant interpretation, but the anatomical details are source interpretations; no artifact photograph or glyph pixels were visually inspected here.

The relationship and chronology among the first-branch graph, 子, and the later sixth-branch graph 巳 remain contested in the dossier’s sources; the opened CUHK page gives one account and does not resolve competing analyses.

The broader semantic chain from child to offspring, honorific, suffix, and seed/fruit is not fully dated or established by the inspected pages. The CUHK entry reports several discrete uses, not a complete chronology.
The Xiaoxuetang 子.6 page failed to open and the applicable official image-rights notice was not verified, so no Xiaoxuetang image is proposed.
The Commons original SVG URL was recovered from the exact file page, but the browser rejected its SVG content type, so image pixels were not visually inspected.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern digital redraw uploaded 2007
items.tradition: Small seal script as represented in the Shuowen-style character project
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 子 in Shuowen seal-script style, a later reference form distinct from the Shang infant-shaped inscriptions.
items.alt: Black seal-script strokes forming 子 centered on a white square.
items.selection_reason: The exact Commons description page identifies the graph and style, links its original image, cites character-data sources, and states public-domain reuse. It provides a later comparison point for the dossier’s reported Shang forms; it is not an artifact photograph.
items.rights: Public domain, as stated on the exact Commons file page.

limitations.text: This candidate is a modern vector drawing of a historical script style, not a photograph or facsimile of a dated inscription; browser rendering failed, so its pixels were not visually checked in this research.

A Xiaoxuetang 子.6 candidate appeared in search results, but its page could not be opened and the exact direct image URL and applicable official rights notice were not verified; it is therefore not proposed.
